groups.title: Testing with Jest
groups.question: Explain how you would test an Express API, from a single function up to a full request.

followUps.Unit Testing — describe, it, expect & Mo: Why mock the database in a unit test instead of using a real one?
followUps.Integration Testing with Supertest: What does a Supertest test catch that a unit test of the handler would miss?

evidence.text: A unit test checks one function on its own, with dependencies like the database replaced by mocks.
Mocks make tests fast and predictable, with no shared data and no dependence on test order.
Real database behaviour is covered by integration tests instead.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (Jest, mock, unit test) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says mocking the database still tests the database queries.

evidence.text: Supertest sends a real HTTP request through the whole Express app in-process.
It catches what a handler-only test misses: middleware order, routing, validation, auth, status codes and the response shape.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (Supertest, integration test) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says Supertest needs the app deployed to a live server.

groups.title: Test Setup & Coverage
groups.question: Explain how you keep a test suite reliable, and how you judge whether it tests enough.

followUps.Test Database Setup & Teardown: Why do tests that share a database pass alone but fail when run together, and how do you stop it?
followUps.Code Coverage & What It Doesn't Guarante: Your code has 100% coverage. Why can it still be badly tested?

evidence.text: Tests sharing a database leave data behind that changes other tests' results.
So they pass alone but fail together, depending on the order they run in.
Reset state for each test: roll back a transaction, truncate tables, or use a fresh test database.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (test database, teardown) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says the fix is to always run the tests in the same order.

evidence.text: Coverage only measures which code ran, not whether the results were checked.
Tests can run every line with weak or no assertions and still reach 100%.
Missing edge cases and wrong expectations don't show up in coverage.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (coverage, 100%) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says 100% coverage means the code has no bugs.

groups.title: API Documentation with OpenAPI
groups.question: Explain how you would document an API so other developers can use it, and keep the docs accurate.

followUps.OpenAPI 3.0 Specification — Paths, Schem: What can tools generate from an OpenAPI spec, and why is a spec that drifts from the code worse than none?
followUps.swagger-jsdoc & Swagger UI Integration: How does writing the docs in comments next to the routes help keep them up to date?

evidence.text: From the spec, tools generate interactive docs, client SDKs, server stubs or request validators.
It is a machine-readable contract of the paths, inputs and responses.
A spec that no longer matches the code sends clients into broken integrations, which is worse than having no docs.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (OpenAPI, Swagger) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says OpenAPI is a testing framework.

evidence.text: The docs are written as comments right next to the route code.
Changing a route means editing the comment in the same place, so it is harder to forget.
The spec is generated from those comments, not maintained by hand.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (swagger-jsdoc, JSDoc) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says the comments are checked against the code, so the docs can never be wrong.

groups.title: Test Strategies
groups.question: Explain how you would test parts of your API that call outside services or need a logged-in user.

followUps.Mocking External Services with Jest Spie: Why not let tests call the real payment or email service, and what replaces it?
followUps.Testing Auth Flows — Protected Route Cov: Which token cases should a protected route's tests cover besides a valid token?

evidence.text: Real calls are slow and flaky, may cost money and can cause real side effects like charges or emails.
The client is replaced with a mock or stub, for example jest.mock or spyOn, that returns fixed responses.
Mocks also let you simulate failures like timeouts or declined payments.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (mock, spy, stub) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says tests should call the real production service to be realistic.

evidence.text: A request with no token or no Authorization header is rejected with 401.
A malformed, tampered or wrongly signed token is rejected.
An expired token is rejected.

notEnough: Only naming the terms (auth tests, JWT) without explaining how they work or why they matter.

misconceptions.text: Says testing with one valid token is enough because the library handles the rest.
